Astra learning/computation branch — 31 October 2026

STATUS

This is an ordinary constructive research note. The main exact-arithmetic
construction has received complementary mathematical reviews. A finite-grid
extension, a centre-only reconstruction, and a cumulative admission construction
are given separately so their interfaces and costs remain visible. Exact rational
and floating-point programs accompany the note. Floating-point experiments do
not certify exact rank, robustness, novelty, or a practical speed advantage.

The central candidate contribution is the combined acquisition theorem:
unknown matrix-algebra acquisition, exact recovery of exhausted multiplicities,
tracial averaging of the remaining multiplicities, and one confidence event for
the entire positive cone of all future expressions. The algebraic ingredients,
Krylov closure, symmetry reduction, and inverse-epsilon single-trace estimation
are established mathematics. Historical novelty of this complete combination
and superiority over a strong retaining algebra learner remain unestablished.

1. SCIENTIFIC QUESTION AND CAPABILITY

Can a computational system acquire operations that support many later, previously
unspecified numerical calculations, instead of relearning each answer? The target
chosen here is a reusable spectral and trace service for a fixed family of large,
possibly dense, full-rank, noncommuting operators. Later questions can contain
new coefficients, sums, products, adjoints, inverses where defined, spectral
functions, and positive matrix pencils. They may be chosen after seeing the
acquired representation and its random probes.

This is a numerical computation interface: a submitted vector v returns A_j v.
It is stronger than passive observations or the scalar-return experimental
interface in Astra N1515/N1521. No physical mechanism for implementing arbitrary
vector queries is inferred from those sources. Every comparator receives the
same vector interface, and every original action is charged.

The valuable regime is small generated algebra rather than small matrix rank.
For example, A_j=U [direct_sum_alpha (B_j,alpha tensor I_malpha)] U*, with hidden
dense U and small noncommuting blocks B_j,alpha, can have rank N for every j.

# Independent proof review: faithful cyclic compression of a Hermitian operator library

## Verdict

The exact theorem is correct. It produces a reusable finite representation of every future expression in a fixed finitely generated matrix *-algebra. The all-future spectral conclusion is stronger than one fitted response, but its mathematical mechanism is established cyclic-subspace / GNS representation theory and simultaneous matrix-* algebra reduction. Novelty cannot be inferred from an independently derived proof.

The genuinely useful question is whether the matrix-free acquisition interface, total costs, and adaptive trace certification produce something beyond existing implementations. The theorem below gives an exact executable acquisition without supplying hidden blocks or a basis as input.

## Fixed library and algebra

Fix Hermitian matrices A_1,...,A_k in C^(N x N) before randomization. Let A be their unital complex *-algebra. Its unitary representation has the form

    A ≅ direct_sum_alpha (M_(r_alpha)(C) tensor I_(m_alpha)).

Write a=dim_C A=sum r_alpha^2 and N=sum r_alpha*m_alpha.

For g in C^N, let K=A g=span{w(A)g: w is a finite word}. If G_alpha is the r_alpha-by-m_alpha reshaping of g's component in block alpha, then

    dim K = sum_alpha r_alpha * rank(G_alpha).

To see this, the alpha block of A g is the image of X -> X G_alpha. Its kernel consists of matrices killing the column space of G_alpha, so its image has dimension r_alpha*rank(G_alpha). Different simple blocks are independently selectable by the central projections of A, and therefore the dimensions add.

Because the A_i are Hermitian, K is reducing. If Q is an orthonormal basis of K, compression rho(X)=Q*XQ is a unital *-homomorphism: XQ=Qrho(X), hence rho(XY)=rho(X)rho(Y) and rho(X*)=rho(X)*.

The restriction in block alpha is M_(r_alpha) acting with multiplicity s_alpha=rank(G_alpha). It is faithful iff s_alpha>0 for every alpha. A Gaussian g has maximal possible rank s_alpha=min(r_alpha,m_alpha), almost surely. Thus

    D=dim K=sum r_alpha min(r_alpha,m_alpha) <= min(N,a).

All simple blocks remain present, so rho is injective. Exact algebraic ranks and traces obtained from central projectors recover the required simple dimensions and represented multiplicities. The coordinate representation is a *-algebra with this G-adjoint. No Cholesky square root is necessary.
